sermon.title: False Shepherds Run
sermon.speaker: Pastor David G. Kincer
sermon.summary: In this message Pastor David G. Kincer teaches from Jeremiah 23 that God judges false shepherds who destroy and scatter His sheep, gathers a remnant, and raises up the righteous Branch of David. He explains how Jesus can be both the Branch and the root, calls the church His body, and ends with a call to balance judgment with hope.
sermon.transcript_source: This transcript comes from YouTube’s automatic English captions, which supply the timing and the words. Punctuation, capitalization and paragraphing were added by hand, and obvious caption errors were corrected; his wording was not rewritten. “[unclear]” marks a word or name that was not clear. Editor note: the pastor names several public figures and religious leaders (including Muhammad, Joseph Smith, Mary Baker, Joel Osteen, Martin Luther, Calvin, Augustine, the Pope and Oprah Winfrey); those names appear in the transcript only, not in the short answers or FAQs. The statistics in the last section (such as marriage rates, single-parent births, the number of wars, and deaths from tobacco and AIDS) are given as spoken, without sources. “Nathaniel,” where he refers to a son of David in Luke’s genealogy, is kept as captioned; Luke 3:31 names Nathan. “Luke 17:21” is followed by a quote that is Jeremiah 23:6. The caption for the passage on being “destroyed for lack of knowledge” read “Hegi chapter 6”; it is marked [unclear] (the words are in Hosea 4:6, shown as quoted only). Five spots are marked [unclear]: that caption, two names after “Joseph Smith,” a number in “Jeremiah [unclear] 23:5,” and one word before “whom you are persecuting.” Caption slips such as “Ma Messiah” and “foottool” were corrected.

chunks.section_question: What is happening in Jeremiah’s day, and why preach hope?
chunks.short_answer: He says Jeremiah preached when God was judging and correcting His people, with wars, captivity, famines, sickness and economic crisis. In the middle of it Jeremiah also speaks “a tremendous word of hope,” and he titles the message about the Messiah: false shepherds run and the sheep run to Jesus.
chunks.text: Jeremiah is preaching at a time when God is judging and punishing, correcting his people. There are wars. There’s a captivity. There are famines and sicknesses. You know, economic crisis is going on all around Jeremiah. And he brings this message just a few years before the first captivity happened. He’s bringing these messages. And in the middle of these messages of punishment, of correction, of wars, of plagues, Jeremiah is also speaking a tremendous word of hope for those who will listen and hear it. Don’t we need hope in the midst of crisis? Yes. And so we’re going to call this when the Messiah comes, false shepherds run and the sheep run to Jesus.

chunks.section_question: Who are the false shepherds who destroy and scatter? (Jeremiah 23:1)
chunks.short_answer: He says Jeremiah 23:1 describes pastors who are destroying and scattering God’s sheep, “the sheep of his pasture.” He says false preachers do not feed people God’s word, do not lead them to Jesus, and “bring them to themselves.” You can tell them, he says, because “they demand that you follow them.”
chunks.text:
Hallelujah. We need the Messiah rising, Jesus Christ. And Jeremiah 23:1: “Woe to the pastors that destroy.” Number one, these pastors, these shepherds are destroying. Number two, they are scattering. Number three, they’re destroying and scattering God’s sheep. And number four, these sheep are the sheep of his pasture. You see the pasture is the place where they are sheep are fed. And these false pro— these false teachers, he deals with prophets in the same chapter, speaks of them in the same way: adulterous men, teaching their own ideas and their own doctrines instead of God’s.

[unclear] chapter 6, it says that we are destroyed for lack of knowledge. And in the New Testament, it says we’re destroyed when we don’t believe in Christ. We’re condemned already because we haven’t believed on the only begotten son of God. It is imperative that the people of the world hear that message that without Jesus that rules out Muhammad and every other source. Without Jesus we will be destroyed, and without his word, the knowledge of his word, we will be destroyed. And that’s what these false preachers do they do not feed the people with the knowledge of God’s word, and God’s people end up being destroyed.

They don’t lead them to Jesus and bring them to Jesus. They bring them to themselves and they wind up being destroyed. Number two, they scatter the flock. These false preachers scatter the flock, and they’re scattering them from Jesus and his word. See, they don’t want them— they bring them to themselves. And it says over in the book of Acts that there will be grievous wolves coming in among you who will draw disciples after themselves. And this is what false shepherds, false pastors do, false so-called evangelists, or whatever title they got. You can tell who they are because they demand that you follow them.

chunks.text:
And they teach things that distract you from Jesus Christ. And his word of righteousness. Amen. This is what these guys do. And we need Jesus. We need his word. And so they scatter from Jesus and his word. Third there, the sheep belong to Jesus. John 10, Jesus said, “I am the good shepherd. My sheep know my voice and I am known of them.” And in Psalms 100, it says, “We are his people and the sheep of his pasture.” And number four, the pasture is Jesus. In John 6:48, Jesus is the bread of life. And in verse 63 of John 6, his word is spirit, his word is truth, his word is life.

And so Jesus feeds us with his word and with himself. How many enjoy feeling and participating in the presence of God when he comes? And then the word. chunks.section_question: What will God do to pastors who harm His flock? (Jeremiah 23:2-3)
chunks.short_answer: He cites Jeremiah 23:2, “I will visit upon them the evil, the harm of their doing,” because they are hurting God’s people. He says there is “no salvation in any other” than Jesus, and that Jesus Himself will gather “the remnant of my flock” back into His fold.
chunks.text:
You know, we bring people to somebody and to somebody’s doctrine instead of Jesus and his doctrine. Amen. And we don’t need those kind of pastors. And God says he’s going to deal with those kind of pastors. Going on in Jeremiah chapter 23:2. Thus saith the Lord against the pastors. I am speaking against the pastors. These pastors that scatter the flock. I will visit upon them the evil, the harm of their doing. See, they’re hurting God’s people. They’re hurting people that don’t even know God because there’s no salvation in any other than who?

Jesus Christ. And the foolishness of preaching is what God has chosen to what? Save those that believe. And so, we got to have the preaching of God’s word. And we got to have Jesus involved. And he says, “I’m against these pastors that hurt and do harm.” Then he goes on to say, “I will gather the remnant of my flock.” He says, “I’m going to gather the remnant of my flock from where I have driven them.” Now, it isn’t the false shepherds that’s scattering them now. It’s Jesus Christ. He has driven them into countries, into areas, and he is going to bring them back out into his fold.

It says there. And so Jesus is going to come and he is going to drive these people that really want him away from these false shepherds, away from these false pastors, these false teachers, and he’s going to bring them where? Into his fold. Hallelujah. And so in the midst of this big mess that Jeremiah is preaching in, there is a tremendous message of hope. And he says this remnant will be fruitful and increase. You see, when we get into God’s pasture where he feeds us with Jesus, the living bread, and his word, the living bread, that word of life, we become fruitful.

chunks.section_question: What is the message of hope in the midst of crisis? (Jeremiah 23:4-5)
chunks.short_answer: He says “we have a message of hope for all Americans” because Jesus is “still Lord in the midst of the judgments.” He says if you are discouraged or fearful, “throw it away,” because Jesus “still has a plan, and nothing can stop him from fulfilling it.”
chunks.text:
Hallelujah. We got a message, church. We have a message in the midst of the darkness that’s in the earth. In the midst of the conflicts that are in the earth, in the midst of the mess that’s in America, we have a message of hope for all Americans. See, he’s still Lord in the midst of the judgments, in the midst of the crisis. He’s still Jesus, the King, the Lord. Then he says, “I will set up shepherds which shall feed them, and they shall no more fear nor be dismayed or be discouraged.” I trust this morning you’re not discouraged because of the message of Christ, the message of how powerful Jesus is keeps you courageous in the midst of very difficult times which we are in in America.

Hallelujah. And if you are discouraged this morning, throw it away. Get rid of that discouragement. If you’re fearful, throw it away. Get rid of your fear. Jesus, in the midst of this mess, is still in control. He still has a plan, and nothing can stop him from fulfilling it. “The days come.” Jeremiah [unclear] 23:5. The days come. Jeremiah says there’s something going to happen in the middle of this mess. There’s some days that are coming that’s going to be tremendous that number one, I will raise up unto David. Okay, King David. So, this guy that’s going to be raised up has to be a descendant of King David.

chunks.section_question: Who are Judah and Israel? (Romans 2:28-29, Galatians 6:15)
chunks.short_answer: He says the promise that “In his days, Judah shall be saved, and Israel shall dwell safely” points to the church. He says a Jew “isn’t the bloodline,” circumcision is “of the heart, the mind, the emotions, the will,” and the followers of Christ are “the real Jew and the real people of Israel,” with Israel and Judah only “a shadow of the real thing to come.”
chunks.text:
“In his days, Judah shall be saved, and Israel shall dwell safely.” Okay?

Now, we’ve taught you this before. Judah, Romans 2:28, a Jew, a person from Judah is not one outwardly, nor circumcision outward in the flesh. See, the Bible says a Jew isn’t the bloodline. And it has nothing to do with circumcision of the flesh. Never did have. It was only shadow laws pointing to the real thing God was going to do. Do you understand, church? And here the scriptures is telling us plainly that a Jew isn’t one outwardly or the bloodline. And circumcision isn’t really circumcision of the flesh. But he is a Jew which is one what? Inwardly. And circumcision is of the heart, the mind, the emotions, the will.

In the what? Spirit. See, we’re born of the spirit. We’re born of the word. This is why born again believers say you got to be born again. The spirit’s got to be involved and change you from a fleshly creature to a new spiritual creature. And God backs up his word and he comes and I don’t care what denomination you’re in. Denominations throw them out. He comes to individuals who seek him. They find him and they obtain what Christ has ordained be in the prophets of old that he would give unto his people. It’s not in the letter. It’s not in book learning. How many of you met people just got a lot of book learning and no substance of the spirit? Yeah.

chunks.section_question: What problems does he point to in America and the world today?

chunks.text:
Hallelujah. And our fruit should imitate the fruit of the one that is our example. He’s right there with us. The church in America seems declining and it seems like the enemies are winning this battle over Jesus and Bible morality. Just like in the days of Jeremiah, we have a drought in the mid states of America. Been that going on for several years. We have an economic decline that we’re in. We have plagues in America, Alzheimer’s, Lyme disease, AIDS, SARS, all these other viruses including the black plague which is rising again in the earth.

See, there are plagues going on, killing thousands of people. Are you out there? We have wars. There’s over 40 wars going on right now at this present time throughout the earth. And we are involved in several of them, indirectly or directly. You see, in the midst of this mess, we’re in an economic difficult time in America. The family unit is broken down. 30% of Americans don’t even bother marrying. Over 40% of children are born to single parent families. The family unit is broken down. The finances is broken down. And we know through history that two main sources of a nation falling is they didn’t handle their money right and they didn’t keep the family strong.

We know that and we’re in the midst of that in America. The number one preventable disease in America, preventable death I should say in America is tobacco. If you don’t smoke, you won’t die early. But we continue to die. You see, the number two is alcohol and drugs. The number three is suicide. Americans are killing themselves. Are you there? And the number four is sexually transmitted diseases, including AIDS, that’s killing over 30,000 people in America, in the North America every year.

And we get all riled up about a gun shooting some kids in a school. We get all riled up the people not having seat belts. And we make everybody wear a seat belts. But we don’t get riled up about these preventable things. We don’t approach them in America and we don’t hold anybody accountable. Breakdown of the family in the world. The number one preventable death cause of death is tobacco in the nations of the world. The number two, you’re not going to believe this, is nourishment. Lack of nourishment. Most of the world don’t have the proper food to eat and they die. The number two death throughout the world is the lack of nourishment, the lack of proper food, and then alcohol, drugs, AIDS.

chunks.section_question: Why must we balance judgment with hope? (Matthew 16:18)
chunks.short_answer: He says God corrects and punishes, but “in the midst of it, he is out to deliver and set people free,” so we cannot get “overloaded on the negative message” and must balance it with hope. He cites Matthew 16:18, “the gates of hell shall not prevail against it,” and says even in our messing up, God says, “You’re my bride.”
chunks.text:
So, we’re in this kind of situation that Jeremiah came with this gospel of hope. And church, I submit to you, we have the message of hope for the world that’s in this kind of situation. In the midst of this, yes, it is God corrects, God punishes, but in the midst of it, he is out to deliver and set people free and bring them out of those those captivities and unto himself and make them fruitful and increase. Amen. That’s the message. So, we can’t get all overloaded on the negative message, the message of correction and judgment. We got to balance it with this message of hope. Could that be true? Matthew 16:18, Jesus said, “I will build my church, and the gates of hell shall not prevail against it.” Did you catch that, church?

The gates of hell will never be victorious over the church, the branch, the remnant. They’ll never be victorious. Oh, we may look downtrodden. We may be in a weak season. We may be messing up. But remember Jeremiah said God is still married to us. Even in our messing up, God says, “You’re my bride.

scriptures.text_nkjv: And I also say to you that you are Peter, and on this rock I will build My church, and the gates of Hades shall not prevail against it.
“Return, O backsliding children,” says the LORD; “for I am married to you. I will take you, one from a city and two from a family, and I will bring you to Zion.

faqs.question: Why does he say we need a message of hope in a crisis?
faqs.answer: He asks, “Don’t we need hope in the midst of crisis?” and answers, “Yes.”

faqs.question: What does he say happens to people without Jesus and his word?
faqs.answer: He says “Without Jesus we will be destroyed, and without his word, the knowledge of his word, we will be destroyed.”

scriptures.text_nkjv: My people are destroyed for lack of knowledge. Because you have rejected knowledge, I also will reject you from being priest for Me; Because you have forgotten the law of your God, I also will forget your children.
“He who believes in Him is not condemned; but he who does not believe is condemned already, because he has not believed in the name of the only begotten Son of God.

faqs.question: What does he say about grievous wolves?
faqs.answer: He says Acts says “there will be grievous wolves coming in among you who will draw disciples after themselves,” and false shepherds are known because “they demand that you follow them.”

scriptures.text_nkjv: For I know this, that after my departure savage wolves will come in among you, not sparing the flock. Also from among yourselves men will rise up, speaking perverse things, to draw away the disciples after themselves.

faqs.question: Why does he say false leaders do not want people coming to Christ?
faqs.answer: He cites John 9:22, where anyone who confessed Jesus as Christ would be put out of the synagogue. He says “they don’t want people coming to Christ.”

scriptures.text_nkjv: His parents said these things because they feared the Jews, for the Jews had agreed already that if anyone confessed that He was Christ, he would be put out of the synagogue.

faqs.question: What does he say about the foolishness of preaching?
faqs.answer: He says God has chosen it to “Save those that believe,” and so “we got to have the preaching of God’s word.”

scriptures.text_nkjv: For since, in the wisdom of God, the world through wisdom did not know God, it pleased God through the foolishness of the message preached to save those who believe.

faqs.question: How does he say we become fruitful?
faqs.answer: He says when we get into God’s pasture where He feeds us with Jesus, the living bread, and His word, “we become fruitful.” He says that is “where we get the power to be fruitful, to do what’s right.”

faqs.question: Did Jesus come to die?
faqs.answer: He says yes: “Yes, he did come to die,” to give His life “that we might be forgiven, that we might be set free, that we might be delivered.”

scriptures.text_nkjv: Pilate therefore said to Him, “Are You a king then?” Jesus answered, “You say rightly that I am a king. For this cause I was born, and for this cause I have come into the world, that I should bear witness to the truth. Everyone who is of the truth hears My voice.”

faqs.question: What does he say matters more than book learning?
faqs.answer: He says the Spirit must be involved to change you “from a fleshly creature to a new spiritual creature,” and that “It’s not in the letter. It’s not in book learning.”

faqs.question: Did people question the virgin birth in Jesus’ day?
faqs.answer: He says yes, and that people still do: “Do they question it today? Absolutely.” He says Luke 3:23 shows people “supposed” Jesus was the son of Joseph.

scriptures.text_nkjv: Now Jesus Himself began His ministry at about thirty years of age, being (as was supposed) the son of Joseph, the son of Heli,

faqs.question: What does he say happens when you know the word and have scriptural answers?
faqs.answer: He says that when God gives you scriptural answers in the midst of a multitude, “They don’t know what to say.”

faqs.question: What does he mean when he says Jesus is the root?
faqs.answer: He says “the root is the source of the rest of the plant,” and Jesus says “I’m the source. I’m the origin of David,” as well as David’s descendant.

scriptures.text_nkjv: “I am the vine, you are the branches. He who abides in Me, and I in him, bears much fruit; for without Me you can do nothing.

faqs.question: Can Christians do anything without Jesus?
faqs.answer: He says no: “Without me, you’ll do nothing.” He says “You won’t even live.”

faqs.question: What does he mean when he says the king is in me?
faqs.answer: He says, “I’m not just a child of the king. The king is in me.” He says we are the branches and the body and temple of Jesus Christ.
